test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: For 14 innings, a cricketer has an average of 51 runs. In the 15th inning, he scores 209 runs. His average score increased by _______. (Round off your answer to the nearest whole number.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the deviation method for averages:

Difference between 15th inning score and old average = 209 − 51 = 158 runs.

This extra score of 158 is distributed equally among all 15 innings.

Increase in average = 158 ÷ 15 = 10.533 runs.

Rounded off to the nearest whole number, the increase is 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 14 innings = 51 runs

Runs scored in 15th inning = 209 runs

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Values ÷ Number of Values

 
 Innings 1 to 14 (Avg: 51) 15th: 51 Extra: +158 
• New Average (61.53) Spread 158 over all 15 innings 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs in 14 innings = 14 × 51 = 714 runs

⇒ Total runs after 15 innings = 714 + 209 = 923 runs

⇒ New average after 15 innings = 923 ÷ 15

⇒ New average = 61.533...

⇒ Increase in average = New average − Old average

⇒ Increase in average = 61.533 − 51 = 10.533

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest whole number, we get 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Batting Average Formula

The batting average is calculated by dividing a cricketer's total runs scored by the number of innings played. Formula: Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Innings.

Inclusion of a New Value (Deviation Method)

When a new value is added to an existing group, the new average can be found directly: New Average = Old Average + (New Value − Old Average) ÷ Total Number of Observations.

Rounding Off Rules

When rounding to the nearest whole number, if the decimal part is 0.5 or higher, we round up to the next integer. Since 10.533 > 10.5, it correctly rounds to 11.
